key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: ACUTE onset over hours to days, often history of gallstones or prior biliary procedures. LOCATION: Right upper quadrant (RUQ), may radiate to right shoulder/scapula. DURATION: CONSTANT pain lasting hours to days. CHARACTER: DULL, ACHING, CONSTANT pain (less severe than cholecystitis alone). AGGRAVATING: No specific aggravating factors. RELIEVING: Nothing relieves pain. TIMING: CONSTANT and progressively worsening. SEVERITY: 5-8/10, moderate to severe. ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: CHARCOT'S TRIAD: fever + jaundice + RUQ pain (50-70%). REYNOLDS' PENTAD: Charcot's triad + hypotension + altered mental status (7-10%, indicates severe disease). High fever with rigors, dark urine, pale stools, pruritus. KEY POSITIVES: Jaundice, high fever, RUQ tenderness, history of gallstones. KEY NEGATIVES: Absence of jaundice makes cholangitis less likely.

red_flags: Hypotension with fever and RUQ pain - septic shock, call 911
Altered mental status with fever and jaundice - severe sepsis, call 911
Rigors (shaking chills) with high fever >103°F - bacteremia
Progressive jaundice with confusion - hepatic encephalopathy risk
